Behind the Screen:
Film Censorship & Self-Censorship in Kazakhstan

New 2026 rule: every film must pass a government review before Kazakh cinemas can show it.

This talk looks behind the official rule, into the real choices of film distributors.

by Nacho (pseudonym) · interpretivist tradition

The Puzzle

ON PAPER

"Advisory"

The law calls the government review "advisory" only — not a final order.
Ministry of Culture and Information of RK, 2026

IN PRACTICE

Cuts. Delays.

In practice: scenes get cut, releases get delayed. Both the government and distributors publicly deny this is "censorship."
Abdrakhmetova, 2026

The gap between the law on paper and what happens in real life is the puzzle.

Research Question

How do film distributors in Kazakhstan navigate pre-release film censorship and scene cuts under the 2026 regulations?

Epistemology · Where I stand

Interpretivism

Understanding personal meaning, not counting numbers.

Focus: how distributors personally explain and make sense of their own decisions.

The camera does not simply record reality — it chooses where to look.

Contribution

What this adds

Global censorship studies — China, Hollywood
KAZAKHSTAN — local distributors, Fall 2026

A small, situated picture: one group — film distributors operating in Kazakhstan — seen in their own words, navigating new 2026 pre-release rules.

"What is the LAW in Kazakhstan?"

Local sources: tell us the official rules and real public cases.

CASE STUDY / TRANSFORMERS
Literature Review · 2 of 2

"How does this WORK in other countries?"

International theory: tells us the hidden mechanics behind rules like this.

Fang (2024)

Multistage gatekeeping + complicit creativity (China).

Lukinbeal (2019)

Fear of losing money drives self-censorship (Hollywood/China).

Bulut (2024)

Public denial, "symbiotic" relationship (Turkey).

THE GAP

We know the law. We know how it works, elsewhere. But no one has asked Kazakh distributors how THEY experience it.

Analytical Framework

Sensitizing Concepts

01 · POWER

State pressure vs. Commercial pressure

02 · GATEKEEPING

What gets shown?

03 · COMPLICIT CREATIVITY

Not as passive, but as active negotiators

They tell me where to look, without fixing what I will find.

What I expect (and could be wrong)
01

Preemptive cuts will be framed as standard business logic, not state pressure.

02

Distributors will describe editing choices in terms of age ratings and box office survival.

03

A tension: wanting artistic integrity vs. needing distribution certificates to protect investment.

Interpretivist does not mean having no expectations.

Where I stand · Positionality

I'm partly an insider

A 2nd-year political science student in Kazakhstan who is an avid moviegoer. Helps me hear local context and public frustration. The risk: I assume cuts are pure censorship before listening.

So I keep my design open. I must listen to how distributors themselves justify their business choices.

Maybe "navigating regulations" turns out to mean commercial survival, not political protest.

Transparency · How I worked with AI

AI HELPED ME

  • Narrow and correct the research question
  • Translate heavy academic jargon into plain English
  • Organize my literature review

I DID

  • Read every source
  • The question and the choices are mine
NOT GRADED

What I understand now, and what I still don't

✓ WHAT I UNDERSTAND

Working with AI helped me clarify my analytical framework so I know exactly what questions to ask during interviews.

? WHAT I STILL DON'T KNOW

Whether distributors will speak openly about state pressure, or if they will only give polished answers. I will only learn how to navigate that silence once I'm in the field.
